lines: Fisherman 1: The sea looks calm today.
Fisherman 2: Calm seas can fool even the oldest sailor. Respect the tide.
Young Fisherman: Tata, if the sky turns orange at dusk, do we sail tomorrow?
Old Fisherman: Sky like ripe mango means fair weather. Sky like dark blood... check your ropes twice.
Old Fisherman: Remember how Mang Tomas repaired his nylon lines?
Young Fisherman: Aye, double-woven near the anchor hook. Never snapped once.
Young Daughter: When Papa comes home, I'll show him this drawing!
School Girl: It's so pretty! The sun looks so warm and yellow.
Young Boy: Quick! Catch that red dragonfly near the banana plant!
School Girl: Careful! Lola says dragonflies bring good luck to the village.
Young Boy: Is Sirena real, Ate?
Young Daughter: Lola says she only sings when the ocean feels lonely for fishermen.
Random Woman: Pahiram ng asin, Mare. The dried galunggong needs a little extra salt today.
Sick Wife: Take whatever you need. Tomas always said neighbors share whatever is in the jar.
Random Woman: Did you hear the church bells ringing early this morning?
Random Guy: Aye, Father Jose was blessing the new fishing nets by the pier.
Random Woman: Manang, I made hot champorado for afternoon merienda. Have a bowl.
Sick Wife: Maraming salamat, Mare. Warm food brings comfort to quiet homes.
Debt Collector: I came to collect ledger debts...
Random Guy: You won't find gold here, sir. But whenever a roof broke, Mang Tomas was first to climb up with bamboo.
Debt Collector: Did Tomas ever leave any coins in his chest?
Old Fisherman: His wealth wasn't in silver, po. It was in the meals he put on his family's table.
